reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the presenter actively promotes paying for OneCoin educational packages and tokens while promising that the purchased tokens can be mined, duplicated through splits, and turned into substantially larger returns. He also encourages recruitment by stating that invited participants' package purchases generate a 10% commission, making the presentation a solicitation built around paid participation and downline income rather than a neutral cryptocurrency lesson. The financial-collapse framing and stated conversion of 5,000 euros into 23,000 euros intensify the solicitation.

citations.quote: if you buy an educational package you have to purchase tokens those tokens you convert them to coins
Those who buy an educational package before the split, will duplicate their tokens.
each package that buy the people I invite pay me one ten percent
In a time of about ninety to one hundred and twenty days, I convert my 5,000 into 23,000
I invite 10 friends in the store and they each buy a 5,000 pack. They give me 10%

opening.argument: The presentation contains explicit consumer-protection language that materially limits how its financial discussion should be understood. The speaker says he does not want to create expectations of making a lot of money, rejects acting from emotion or ignorance, and tells listeners to educate themselves before doing anything. He also says the activity is not a stock-market business promising monthly income. Those are unusually direct cautions against treating the talk as a guaranteed-return solicitation; they support reading it as an educational discussion with personal examples and uncertainty rather than a deceptive promise.

citations.quote: I don't want to generate in the people an expectation for them to make a lot of money
don't come here because of emotion don't approach us with ignorance If you're going to do something, do so by educating yourself and knowing how you're doing
No, we are anti-credits and debt.
invest and you will get a monthly income

rebuttal.rebuttal: The package and token discussion does not erase the speaker's express warning against expectation, debt, and uninformed action. The claimed 5,000-to-23,000 figure is presented as a personal strategy and projection, while the speaker expressly distinguishes the activity from a business paying monthly income. The prosecution therefore treats an explicitly qualified discussion as an unconditional promise.

citations.quote: That is one of the reasons for which I have invested 5,000
I don't want to generate in the people an expectation for them to make a lot of money

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning does not neutralize the presentation's concrete financial inducements. The speaker simultaneously says packages require token purchases, tokens become coins, and buying before a split duplicates them. Saying not to expect money cannot make those specific earning representations merely educational.

citations.quote: if you buy an educational package you have to purchase tokens those tokens you convert them to coins
Those who buy an educational package before the split, will duplicate their tokens.

opening.argument: The dominant format is a classroom-style explanation of money, cryptocurrency, algorithms, mining, and market mechanics. The speaker describes OneCoin as based on financial education, explains how an algorithm can generate coins, and contrasts cryptocurrency with earlier payment systems. The visual evidence likewise shows a presenter addressing seated attendees beside a projector and whiteboard, consistent with a seminar and demonstration. A presentation that teaches concepts and illustrates the speaker's own experience should not automatically be classified as a solicitation merely because commercial examples appear within the lesson.

citations.quote: One Coin is a company that is based on financial education.
I'll give you an example. Let's suppose I want to create a cryptocurrency
The algorithm produces 120 million of coins.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational setting is relevant context, but it does not change the substance of the lesson. The speaker moves from explaining cryptocurrency to telling attendees what package to buy, how tokens are converted, and what returns he expects. Calling those demonstrations cannot remove their direct commercial message.

citations.quote: if you buy an educational package you have to purchase tokens those tokens you convert them to coins
In a time of about ninety to one hundred and twenty days, I convert my 5,000 into 23,000

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A seminar format is compatible with a promotional pitch; it does not make the pitch neutral. The alleged lesson repeatedly links access to paid educational packages with tokens, mining, and financial outcomes. The algorithm example also does not establish that the offered system actually produces the represented returns.

citations.quote: you have to buy an educational package
the company gives you tokens if you buy an educational package
You are going to duplicate your tokens and mine and get a profit-ability of 1982 euros.

opening.argument: The material can be read as promotion of a paid educational product with associated tokens and a referral compensation plan, which is ordinary commercial activity rather than proof of a scam. The speaker describes package levels, token conversion, and a commission arrangement openly, and even explains that commissions may be partly paid in cash and partly in tokens. The record does not show a request for passwords, identity documents, or other credentials, nor does it establish an independently verified loss or failed withdrawal. The judge should not infer those missing mechanisms from the mere presence of prices, purchases, or referrals.

citations.quote: What this company does to become a part of the One Coin community is that you have to buy an educational package
each package that buy the people I invite pay me one ten percent
40% of this 5000 that I get in token
the other 60% are cash

rebuttal.rebuttal: Ordinary commerce does not explain why the purchase is tied to token mining, splits, and sharply increased value. The speaker does more than describe a product: he recommends a 5,000-euro strategy, repeats the claimed conversion into 23,000, and gives an example of earning commissions from ten recruits. Those are the operative inducements, not incidental retail details.

citations.quote: In a time of about ninety to one hundred and twenty days, I convert my 5,000 into 23,000
I invite 10 friends in the store and they each buy a 5,000 pack. They give me 10%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a credential request or documented loss is not decisive. The relevant mechanism is visible in the speaker's own account: payment for packages leads to tokens, tokens are mined or duplicated, and recruits' purchases produce commissions. That is a paid-return and recruitment structure, not ordinary merchandise supported by a conventional deliverable.
